title: Cyclic specialization: cyc(rotation r) = gcd(n, r) and the necklace count
content: The header states the parent's explicit request (openQuestions[0]): recover the concrete cyclic value cyc(rotation r) = gcd(n, r) from the abstract group-agnostic Burnside formula |Fix(g)| = k^cyc(g). Three results are delivered: (A) cyc(rotation r) = gcd(n, r) — the rotation r decomposes the n positions into exactly gcd(n,r) cycles; (B) #(colorings fixed by rotation r) = k^{gcd(n,r)}, immediate from (A) and the parent's per-element count; (C) the classical cyclic necklace count ∑_{r:ZMod n} k^{gcd(n,r)} = (#necklaces up to rotation)·n. The rotation group is written multiplicatively as Rot n = Multiplicative (ZMod n) acting on itself so the parent's multiplicative machinery applies verbatim. Verified: 0 sorries, 0 axioms (only propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound, no native_decide).

title: Rot n = Multiplicative (ZMod n) acting on itself by rotation
content: The cyclic group of n rotations is written multiplicatively as `Rot n := Multiplicative (ZMod n)` and acts on itself — the n necklace positions — by left translation g • x = g * x, i.e. rotation. The rotation by r is `rotation r := Multiplicative.ofAdd r`. This multiplicative framing is the key reuse trick: the parent's cyc, card_fixedBy_eq_pow_cyc, and Burnside averaging are stated for [Group G] [MulAction G X], so taking G = X = Rot n with the regular self-action lets them apply with no re-derivation. `card_rot` records that the necklace has Nat.card (Rot n) = n positions (Multiplicative is a type synonym for ZMod n, whose Fintype card is n).

title: (A) cyc(rotation r) = gcd(n, r): orbit quotient = coset space, then Lagrange
content: The conceptual heart. `card_zpowers_rotation` computes the cyclic subgroup size |⟨rotation r⟩| = orderOf (ofAdd r) = addOrderOf r = n / gcd(n,r), via Nat.card_zpowers, orderOf_ofAdd_eq_addOrderOf, and ZMod.addOrderOf_coe (applied after rewriting r = ↑r.val with ZMod.natCast_zmod_val). `cyc_rotation` then identifies the ⟨r⟩-orbit quotient with the coset space using Mathlib's equivSubgroupOrbitsQuotientGroup — valid because the regular translation action is pretransitive (Regular.isPretransitive) and cancellative (IsCancelSMul for a CancelMonoid) — so cyc(rotation r) = ⟨r⟩.index (Subgroup.index_eq_card). Finally Lagrange (Subgroup.card_mul_index) gives (n/d)·index = n with d = gcd(n,r) ∣ n; since n = (n/d)·d, cancelling the positive factor n/d (Nat.eq_of_mul_eq_mul_left) yields index = d = gcd(n,r).
prerequisites: orbit ↔ coset for free transitive actions

title: (B) Fixed colorings = k^{gcd(n,r)}
content: `card_fixedColorings_rotation` is the headline necklace fact: the number of k-colorings of the n-bead necklace fixed by rotation r is k^{gcd(n,r)}. It is one rewrite — apply the parent's card_fixedBy_eq_pow_cyc (which gives k^{cyc(rotation r)}) and substitute (A). This is exactly the classical 'a rotation with gcd(n,r) cycles fixes k^{gcd(n,r)} colorings', now obtained as a specialization of the general orbit-count rather than a separate computation.

title: (C) Cyclic necklace counting via Burnside averaging
content: `sum_pow_gcd_eq_card_necklaces_mul` recovers the classical necklace formula in integer form: ∑_{r:ZMod n} k^{gcd(n,r)} = (#necklaces up to rotation)·n. The proof reindexes the parent's averaging identity sum_pow_cyc_eq_card_orbits_mul_card — a sum over g : Rot n — along the equiv Multiplicative.toAdd : Rot n ≃ ZMod n (Fintype.sum_equiv), rewriting each term k^{cyc g} to k^{gcd(n,(toAdd g).val)} via (A). Dividing by n gives the usual (1/n)·∑_r k^{gcd(n,r)} count of k-colored n-bead necklaces.
